# Team Management — Migrations

**Status:** Not hand-written. Auto-generated by **drizzle-kit**, same convention as `reviews-2026-07-06/migrations/README.md`.

## How migrations are produced

The team-management schema is defined across two new/modified schema files:

- `src/modules/auth/schema.ts` — modified (`users` gains `personId`, `roleId`, `invitedAt`, `mfaEnforcedAt`; `sessions` gains `label`)
- `src/modules/team/schema.ts` — new (`roles`, `permissions`, `role_permissions`)
- `src/modules/auth/mfa/schema.ts` — new (`user_mfa`, `user_backup_codes`)

All three are re-exported through the aggregated barrel at `src/lib/db/schema/index.ts`:
```ts
export * from "@/modules/team/schema";
export * from "@/modules/auth/mfa/schema";
```

drizzle-kit diffs the aggregated schema against the current migration set, so the migration SQL is generated by running:

```sh
npm run db:generate   # -> drizzle-kit generate
```

This drops a new numbered migration under `drizzle/` (the existing set is `0000`–`0031+`), covering the new tables, new columns, FKs, and indexes.

## Applying

```sh
npm run db:migrate     # -> drizzle-kit migrate
# or, for a clean local reset:
npm run seed:reset     # drops data/dev.db*, migrates, seeds
```

## Schema.ts deltas (source of truth — NOT checked-in SQL)

### `src/modules/auth/schema.ts` — `users` additions
```ts
// existing columns unchanged; add:
personId: text("person_id"),              // nullable FK -> people.id (link, don't merge)
roleId: text("role_id"),                  // nullable FK -> roles.id (null = legacy enum role)
invitedAt: integer("invited_at"),         // when the invite email was sent (for expiry display)
mfaEnforcedAt: integer("mfa_enforced_at"),// when org-wide MFA enforcement began counting grace
// role enum column KEPT as a denormalized "system class" cache (owner|editor|custom)
//   — never the sole source of truth once roleId is set; always set both together in actions.
```

### `src/modules/auth/schema.ts` — `sessions` addition
```ts
label: text("label"),   // optional device label ("Chrome on macOS") shown in session mgmt UI
```

### `src/modules/team/schema.ts` — new
```ts
export const roles = sqliteTable("roles", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey().$defaultFn(createId),
  name: text("name").notNull().unique(),        // "Owner", "Editor", or custom "Content Lead"
  description: text("description").notNull().default(""),
  isSystem: integer("is_system", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull().default(false), // system roles immutable
  requireMfa: integer("require_mfa", { mode: "boolean" }).notNull().default(false),
  createdAt: integer("created_at").notNull().$defaultFn(() => Date.now()),
});

export const permissions = sqliteTable("permissions", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey().$defaultFn(createId),
  key: text("key").notNull().unique(),          // "team:manage", "content:publish", ...
  description: text("description").notNull().default(""),
});

export const rolePermissions = sqliteTable("role_permissions", {
  roleId: text("role_id").notNull(),
  permissionId: text("permission_id").notNull(),
}, (t) => ({ pk: primaryKey({ columns: [t.roleId, t.permissionId] }) }));
```

### `src/modules/auth/mfa/schema.ts` — new
```ts
export const userMfa = sqliteTable("user_mfa", {
  userId: text("user_id").primaryKey(),         // 1:1 with users
  secret: text("secret").notNull(),             // AES-256-GCM encrypted (iv:ct:tag, base64)
  enabledAt: integer("enabled_at").notNull().$defaultFn(() => Date.now()),
});

export const userBackupCodes = sqliteTable("user_backup_codes", {
  id: text("id").primaryKey().$defaultFn(createId),
  userId: text("user_id").notNull(),
  codeHash: text("code_hash").notNull().unique(), // SHA-256 of the raw code (single-use)
  usedAt: integer("used_at"),
  createdAt: integer("created_at").notNull().$defaultFn(() => Date.now()),
});
```

## Indexes to declare in schema.ts

- `roles.name` — unique (above).
- `permissions.key` — unique (above).
- `role_permissions` — composite PK (above).
- `user_backup_codes.userId` — index (lookup-all-for-user on regenerate).
- `users.roleId` — index (resolve permissions by role).
- `users.personId` — index (reverse lookup: which staff account is linked to this person).

## Seed plan (NOT a migration — a seed script)

System roles + the permission catalog are seeded, not migrated, matching how `people` defaults work. New seed file: `seed/team.ts` (or extend `seed/neutral.ts`), invoked by `npm run seed` / `npm run seed:reset`.

Seed contents:
1. **Permission catalog** — insert all keys from `src/modules/team/permissions.ts` (idempotent upsert by `key`).
2. **System roles** — insert `Owner`, `Editor`, `Author`, `Moderator`, `Viewer` with `isSystem: true` (idempotent upsert by `name`).
3. **System role → permission assignments** — populate `role_permissions` for each system role (idempotent: delete + re-insert for system roles on each seed run, so permission edits in code propagate).

**Existing-user backfill:** for every existing `users` row, set `roleId` to the matching system role's id (`owner` → Owner role, `editor` → Editor role). This is a one-time seed step guarded by `roleId IS NULL`, so it runs once and never re-touches users who have been moved to custom roles.

## Implementation checklist

- [ ] Add the schema.ts deltas above; re-export through `src/lib/db/schema/index.ts`.
- [ ] Run `npm run db:generate`; review the generated SQL for the new tables, columns, FKs, and indexes.
- [ ] Run `npm run db:migrate` against dev (`data/dev.db`).
- [ ] Write `seed/team.ts`; run `npm run seed:reset`; verify system roles + permissions + existing-user backfill landed.
- [ ] Spot-check with a read query: `SELECT name, is_system FROM roles;` and `SELECT key FROM permissions ORDER BY key;`.
- [ ] Commit the generated migration alongside the schema in the same PR.

## Postgres-swap-clean invariant

All schema uses `sqliteTable` + standard `text`/`integer` columns + `primaryKey` composite helper — no raw SQL types, no SQLite-only constructs. The `mode: "boolean"` integer mapping is already used elsewhere in the codebase (e.g. `data-sources`) and is Postgres-swap-safe. See `docs/recipes/swap-database-to-postgres.md`.
